thread.title: 10 Stocks Investors Raced to Buy During February's Brutal Market Correction

author: thestreet.com
title: 10 Stocks Investors Raced to Buy During February's Brutal Market Correction
text:
Sensing an opportunity that hasn't presented itself too many times since the Great Recession ended, investors pounced in February.
TD Ameritrade clients appeared to use the pullback in stocks last month as a buying opportunity, the online brokerage house revealed Monday in its latest investor movement index summary. Unsurprisingly, investors gravitated to big-cap stocks with the most widely recognized names.
Stocks That Were Net Buys in February General Electric ( GE ) and Ford ( F ) caught interest after shares hovered around multi-year lows, TD Ameritrade said.
Action Alerts Plus holdings Apple ( AAPL ) and Amazon ( AMZN ) were bought after shares were sold despite solid fourth-quarter earnings from each.
Boeing ( BA ) , 2017's hottest component in the Dow Jones Industrial Average, was a net buy.
Action Alerts Plus holding Microsoft ( MSFT ) received interest as it continued to execute on its turnaround under CEO Satya Nadella.
Off some 20% from its recent highs, Chinese internet search giant Alibaba ( BABA ) was a net buy in the month.
Other popular names, according to TD Ameritrade, included Action Alerts Plus holding Nvidia ( NVDA ) , Berkshire Hathaway ( BRK.A ) and Netflix ( NFLX ) . Netflix continues to be one of the hottest names in the market , and is up 50% year to date.
Stocks That Were Net Sells in February Not every big-cap stock caught the attention of bottom fishers, however.
Action Alerts Plus holding Facebook's ( FB ) stock was a net sell after concerns arose over changes to its news feed.
Target ( TGT ) was net sold as investors grew fearful about fourth-quarter earnings following Walmart's ( WMT ) surprising earnings miss .
Bristol-Myers Squibb ( BMY ) was net sold after its stock reached an 18-month high.
